The eight-tables, first-royal-female-teacher, live-ostrich, first-female-teacher, unopposed-political-participation, 120 CE death, and strong Nujie reception claims remain source-scoped.

claims.statement: [[zizhi-tongjian-hanji-705-5-banzhao-xubian-hanshu-shibi-qianqiu-diyi-ren-ljueol3mogwfh-d-w4fs7jzp0h9e|Hanji 705-5]] and [[zizhi-tongjian-hanji-705-6-banzhao-sanci-yimingjingren-guimi-ganzheng-no-1-lpnprzwqh6c7jqcy7cxpgganibmm|Hanji 705-6]] together add a source-scoped gendered education and reception case: [[BanZhaoLateHan]]'s authority starts in Ban-family learning through [[BanBiaoEasternHan]], becomes public when [[EmperorHeOfHan]] summons her to Dongguan to finish [[BanGuEasternHan]]'s unfinished `Han Shu` tables and teach the text, then extends into palace women education, advice to [[EmpressDowagerDengLateHan]], memorial advocacy for [[BanChaoEasternHan]], and later [[NujieGenderNormTransmission]] afterlife. [[MaRongLateHan]], [[FemaleCourtEducationEasternHan]], [[CourtWomenHistoriography]], and [[BanJieyuWesternHan]] keep the case tied to scholarly transmission, court education, dynastic historiography, and Western Han female-literary memory rather than private talent alone.

qualifications: Source-scoped to the U.S. clerical-worker movement described in the Planet Money episode.
The source links mass recognition to the film and song but also stresses that many demands remained unresolved and unionization later declined.
claims.statement: The 9to5 branch makes [[OfficeWorkerLaborOrganizing]] part of [[WomenWorkplaceProgressStall]]: [[NineToFiveOrganization|9to5]] turned everyday clerical-worker grievances under [[GenderedOfficeHierarchy]] into demands around pay, promotion, pregnancy protection, child care, harassment, leave, and union leverage rather than treating them as individual office complaints.

qualifications: The episode is conceptual and interview-based; it does not supply a measured enterprise rollout comparison.
Behavioral metrics can become misleading if separated from frontline interviews and workflow context.
claims.statement: Workplace AI adoption depends on trust, participation, and observed behavior: EP43 argues that [[InstitutionalTrustAIAdoption]], [[CognitiveDiversityAIAdoption]], [[AIAdoptionBehavioralSignals]], [[AIOverwriteRate]], and [[QuietAIAdoptionDeparture]] reveal whether tools are changing work beyond deployment activity.

qualifications: The claim is secondary because the source is a text-reading, not a modern workplace or education study.
The source-scoped conduct lesson should not be generalized into passivity or into a complete theory of social mobility.
The text attribution and metaphysical vocabulary remain bounded to Hanji 733-3.
claims.statement: [[zizhi-tongjian-hanji-733-3-juju-jieshi-qiangu-mingyan-qijie-quan-ni-yiding-yao-du-lkck6rsfd-xtzwipdy-stdhwebey|Hanji 733-3]] adds a secondary work-and-society conduct case: [[HanyaoFu]] and [[FateTimingExternalConditions]] frame achievement, rank, and blocked effort as condition-dependent, so the practical response is self-possession in adversity and humility in prosperity rather than reducing outcomes to talent, ambition, or labor; [[LyuMengzheng]] anchors the attribution while [[FortuneMisfortuneReversal]] supplies the neighboring reversal logic.

qualifications: The evidence is a source-scoped Alpha School account rather than comparative school-system proof.
The strongest performance, SAT, voucher, learning-rate, Founder School, GT Squared, and lower-cost-school claims are not independently validated in the source.
The model may involve selection, family-resource, cost, implementation, and generalization issues not resolved by the episode.
claims.statement: The Alpha School episode adds a modern education-institution claim: [[AIMasteryLearningModel]], [[RemedialEducationTargeting]], [[WorkingMemoryLearningBottleneck]], [[EducationMotivationArchitecture]], and [[BuilderBasedSchoolDay]] frame school improvement as matching level, motivation, human guidance, and applied environments, not just more content or app access.

qualifications: The source reports the China and Nigeria education results secondhand, so study design and external validity remain bounded to the episode summary.
The contrast supports an implementation claim rather than a universal AI benefit or a screen-free ban.
Homework-score gains are weaker evidence than exam transfer when tools can complete practice work for students.
claims.statement: [[after-the-flood-nepals-ongoing-rescue-6a969d560cefab2730527078|After the flood]] qualifies the AI education thread: [[AIAsTutor]] can support learning when it changes practice, but [[AIHomeworkTransferGap]] and [[AIShortcutRisk]] show that AI homework help can raise submitted work while weakening exam transfer if students outsource the effort. The [[China]] and [[Nigeria]] contrast keeps [[LearningHowToLearn]] and [[HumanJudgmentUnderAI]] focused on implementation and active practice.

qualifications: This is a source-scoped reading of a drama and interview episode, not a general theory of film labor, psychotherapy, family repair, or AI production.
The Alzheimer and forgetting comments remain reflective metaphors rather than clinical evidence.
claims.statement: EP281 adds a creative-work and society case: [[ChanDrama]], [[WuZhenyu]], and [[YuanYumei]] connect [[EmbodiedActingImprovisation]], [[TemporaryFamilyHealing]], [[HumanImperfectionCreativeValue]], and [[LoveAsContainingFrame]] to work that depends on body, location, scene response, imperfect human taste, and relations that can hold fear, grief, anger, aging, and damage; AI is useful only as production assistance, not as a replacement for human feeling.

qualifications: The claim is source-scoped to one The Intelligence episode and should not be read as a comprehensive account of Hollywood labor, contracts, or AI adoption.
The examples show workflow adoption and production assistance more clearly than wholesale replacement of performers or crews.
Likeness, disclosure, quality, and labor reactions remain legitimacy constraints rather than resolved policy outcomes.
claims.statement: The Intelligence source adds a work-and-society AI-production case: [[GenerativeAIHollywoodProduction]], [[AIVideoProductionWorkflow]], [[LiveActionFilmUnderAI]], and [[CreativeLaborAIBacklash]] show generative AI entering Hollywood through previsualization, stunt and effects safety, editing, dubbing, and hidden workflow use while [[SyntheticPerformers]], [[AIPublicLikenessGeneration]], and [[AIContentProvenance]] keep replacement claims bound by trust, rights, and disclosure.

qualifications: Source-scoped to the Marketplace Tech interview with Jamie Siminoff; TAKE implementation proof, downstream legal handling after police sharing, bystander consent, and actual household adoption remain unresolved.
claims.statement: [[tech-20260901-0901-mp-tech-pod-128-tech-20260901-0901-mp-tech-pod-128|Ring Moves to Make Its Video Footage More Private]] adds a work-and-society edge: [[RingTakeEncryption]], [[ConsumerCameraSurveillance]], and [[PublicSafetyPrivacyTradeoff]] show that household AI camera features become social infrastructure when police requests, shared users, bystanders, and future-use anxiety shape trust beyond technical capability.

qualifications: This is a family, clinical, and public-education edge inside rehabilitation episodes, not school-policy, parenting, swallowing treatment, articulation treatment, or individualized medical advice.
Home scaffolding and environmental adjustments do not replace professional assessment; family capacity, time, cost, care access, and patient-specific prognosis remain source-scoped.

VOL.34's adult dysphagia, botulinum-toxin, gastrostomy, thickener, soft-food, and care-pathway claims remain source-scoped; VOL.35's child-development signals and music-cue examples remain source-scoped.
claims.statement: VOL.34 and VOL.35 add a work-and-society edge around rehabilitation as scaffolded communication and feeding environments: [[SpeechLanguageRehabilitation]] covers swallowing, eating, articulation, aphasia, and child language delay, while [[DysphagiaRehabilitationSafety]], [[FunctionalArticulationDisorder]], [[FamilyCommunicationScaffolding]], [[ChildCommunicationDevelopmentSignals]], and [[PediatricLanguageDelayEarlyIntervention]] show that progress depends on clinical assessment, caregiver practice opportunities, texture and posture adjustments, response habits, and professional escalation rather than diction polish, folk reassurance, or generic training.

qualifications: The episode summarizes policy contours rather than the complete official rule, enforcement design, vendor policy, or teacher-training plan.
The claim is an education-governance synthesis, not evidence that school AI restrictions improve outcomes by themselves.
claims.statement: [[tech-20260904-0904-mp-tech-pod-128-tech-20260904-0904-mp-tech-pod-128]] adds a school-system AI policy case: [[NewYorkCityPublicSchools]], [[SchoolAIBoundaries]], and [[AIGuidedLearningGuardrails]] show that education institutions may restrict AI access, screens, grading, and companion-style use to preserve student work and adult judgment, while the same source keeps AI literacy and home-device exposure unresolved.

summary: The New York City school AI-policy segment adds an institutional learning-boundary edge: schools can restrict AI access, screens, grading, and companion-style use to preserve student work and adult judgment, but still need explicit AI literacy and cannot control home-device exposure. The coffee-bean footwear episode adds a narrow everyday-life consumption edge: comfort shoes, ballet-sneaker hybrids, and seasonal footwear now blur work, school, commuting, sport, and casual settings by preserving comfort while making silhouettes look more refined. VOL.34 adds a speech-and-swallowing rehabilitation edge: speech therapy covers eating, swallowing, articulation, aphasia, cognition, and communication, and its social value depends on clinical assessment, team coordination, posture and texture adjustments, assistive routines, family expectation management, and source-scoped escalation boundaries rather than diction polish or generic self-training. The sleep toolkit adds a narrow work-and-society edge: wake-time consistency, morning and evening light, caffeine delay, temperature cues, naps, and phase-shifting practices shape alertness and recovery under ordinary schedules, travel, or shift work, but remain public health education rather than workplace prescription. VOL.208 adds a worker/listener health-boundary edge: headphone-heavy podcast listening and editing become work-and-society material when volume, duration, sudden audio peaks, noisy environments, device fit, canal pressure, hygiene, and warning symptoms shape whether a media habit becomes a health risk. VOL.35 pairs with VOL.34 on the family-and-child-development edge: speech-language rehabilitation depends partly on caregivers creating communication opportunities, reducing passive screen or overcare patterns, observing comprehension and gesture signals, and coordinating with professional assessment. Hanji 697 and Hanji 703 add source-scoped institution and role-boundary analogies: civil restoration, trust under accusation, talent deployment, and pressured allegiance show capability as role- and institution-bound. Hanji 705-5 and Hanji 705-6 together add a source-scoped Eastern Han gendered education and historiography case: [[BanZhaoLateHan]] now links Ban-family learning, [[BanGuEasternHan]] unfinished `Han Shu`, [[EmperorHeOfHan]] Dongguan commission, palace teaching, advice to [[EmpressDowagerDengLateHan]], memorial advocacy for [[BanChaoEasternHan]], [[MaRongLateHan]] student layer, [[BanJieyuWesternHan]] memory, [[CourtWomenHistoriography]], and the disputed [[NujieGenderNormTransmission]] afterlife. [[after-the-flood-nepals-ongoing-rescue-6a969d560cefab2730527078|After the flood]] adds an AI education qualification: AI help needs active transfer into exam performance rather than homework shortcuts. The broader topic continues to show work, education, and social capacity as institution-bound rather than trait-bound: Hanji 725-813 and 1056-1060 treat office roles, family status, counsel, succession, reputation, and access channels as sources of capability or exposure; modern workplace and labor sources connect boundaries, evidence, hidden rules, bullying, clerical organizing, creator monetization, finance-career risk, lifestyle cost discipline, and occasion norms; education sources emphasize self-testing, effort, fieldwork, mastery, motivation, and builder practice; AI, product, and creative-work sources show adoption requiring workflow fit, trust, distribution, verification, embodied judgment, and human taste; health, exercise, and rehabilitation sources frame public education through need assessment, risk boundaries, clinical limits, and environment design. Across the input, durable agency comes from grounded feedback loops, social trust, realistic constraints, and environments that let people act well rather than from hype, rank, followers, fluent answers, or capability claims alone. The Ring privacy episode adds a society-facing technology-adoption branch: domestic AI cameras move toward public-safety workflows only when household consent, user key control, optional sharing, and future-use anxieties are recognized.
title: Work, Education, and Society
